# ScreenGui

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ScreenGui")`

The root of a tree of UI drawn on the screen. Parent it to `UIService`. Everything under it is laid out against the window and drawn over the world.

Layout is computed per `ScreenGui`, and only when something under it changes. A screen where nothing changed costs no layout work.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayOrder` | `number` | `0` | read/write | Which `ScreenGui` is drawn on top where two overlap: the one with the higher value. `ZIndex` orders objects within a tree, and this orders the trees. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this tree is laid out and drawn. A disabled `ScreenGui` costs nothing. |
| `KeepOnSceneLoad` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether this screen is kept when the game changes scene, instead of being removed with the scene it is in. A loading screen shown before `SceneService:LoadScene` stays up while the scene changes, and a script removes it on `SceneLoaded`. |
| `Player` | `Player?` | `nil` | read/write | The local player this interface belongs to. With a player set, the interface is laid out in that player's view when the window is split, it has its own selection (`SelectedObject`), and only that player's gamepad (`Player.GamepadId`) navigates it. Four players can each pick a card at the same time.<br><br>With nil, the interface belongs to everyone: it covers the whole window and is navigated by `UIService.GamepadId`. When the player leaves, the interface is hidden until it is given another player or nil. |
| `ReferenceHeight` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The window height this interface was designed for, or 0 to work in pixels. When it is set, every offset, text size, corner radius and stroke under it is measured in units of a window that tall, and the whole tree is scaled to the actual window. A layout designed at 720 then takes up the same share of a phone screen with twice the pixels, instead of half.<br><br>The width follows from the window's aspect ratio, so anchor to edges with `Scale` and size with `Offset`. `AbsolutePosition` and `AbsoluteSize` stay in window pixels. 720 suits a layout designed on a desktop. |
| `ScreenInsets` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this tree is laid out inside `UIService.SafeAreaInsets` instead of against the whole window. On by default, so that a HUD is not hidden by a screen cutout. Turn it off for a background that should fill the screen. |
| `SelectedObject` | `UIObject?` | `nil` | read/write | The object this player's gamepad has selected in this interface. It is used only when `Player` is set; otherwise `UIService.SelectedObject` is used. |
| `XRDistance` | `number` | `1.5` | read/write | In a headset, how far in front of the player's head this interface is shown, in meters. In a headset there is no screen to draw over, so each `ScreenGui` is a flat panel in front of the player instead, pointed at with a controller. Flat, it is not used. |
| `XRFollow` | `Enum.XRFollow` | `Enum.XRFollow.Lazy` | read/write | In a headset, how this interface's panel follows the head: always (`Head`), once the head has turned more than 30 degrees away (`Lazy`), or never (`Fixed`). |
| `XRPixelsPerMetre` | `number` | `1000` | read/write | In a headset, how many of this interface's pixels make a meter of its panel. The panel is 1280 by 720 pixels, or `ReferenceHeight` tall and 16:9 wide when that is set: 1.28 meters wide at the default. A higher value makes a smaller, sharper panel. |
